newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission seeks fines on Germany, Italy over green laws.
newsitem.headline: Commission seeks fines on Germany, Italy over green laws.

text.p: The European Commission asked the European Court on Wednesday to fine Germany and Italy for non compliance with EU environmental law.

"The European Commission decided to make applications to the European Court of Justice against Germany and Italy for failing to comply with previous court judgements for infringing European Union environmental law," a statement said.

"It also decided that in making these applications, it will for the first time ask the court to impose financial penalties which the court obtained the power to do under the Maastricht treaty," it said.
The daily penalties against Germany, which relate to rules on protection of birds, ground and surface water, are for 26,400 Ecus, 264,000 Ecus and 158,400 Ecus respectively.
The Commission proposed daily fines for Italy related to waste and radiation protection of 123,900 Ecus and 159,300 Ecus.

"I see it as extremely important that the Commission here for the first time has come out with proposals for financial penalties. These cases will serve as important precendents," said European Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard in statement IP/97/63.

One Commission official, who asked not to be named, said that about 30 infringement cases against the EU's 15 countries, including the five cases now subject to proposed fines, were under consideration for fines action.
Among those files closest to a decision were four cases against Belgium, one against Greece, one against Luxembourg and six against France, the official said.
No country will be liable for any payments until the Court upholds the Commission's applications, which it might not even consider for months.
"It could take quite a while unfortunately," Bjerregaard's spokesman Peter Jorgensen told a news conference.
